changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `db11afd49` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1763 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2369 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36618166344)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5b92f7ab4309a4f6926ad1fb7e00a992ae9ab954`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11124 (body, triage `5895688948`, claim `5895871015`, os-dev-report `5897040620`), PR #11135 (body, 3 files, net diff against `main`), the latest check-runs on the head, and head-revision reads of `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, `preview-registry.ts`, `FlowPreview.tsx`, `FlowCanvas.tsx`, the `FlowInspector` family and `metadata-admin/i18n.ts` for context. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface / accept-set: nothing moves — right.** `AutomationsPillar`'s props are unchanged (`packageId`, `publishNonce`, `onDraftSaved`, `readOnly`); no export, type, schema, accepted value or i18n key is added. The only new i18n use is the existing `engine.studio.pkg.readonlyHint` (present at the head, en and zh-CN), the same string the Studio header already shows on a read-only package.
- **The switch — right.** `disabled={!isEditable || !!saving || readOnly}` with the read-only hint as its title, and `toggleEnabled` returns early on `!current || readOnly` (`readOnly` added to its deps). `isEditable` is `!!Preview` (registry populated), never a server flag, so before this diff nothing disabled the switch on a read-only package — the card's symptom 1. The early return is the Data pillar's own `addField` shape (`if (readOnly) return;`): belt-and-braces, one mechanism.
- **The inspector — right, one mechanism.** `readOnly: false` becomes `readOnly,` — the same shape the Data pillar hands its object inspector (objectui#2259). `FlowInspector` spreads its props into `FlowNodeInspector` / `FlowEdgeInspector`, both of which destructure `readOnly` and set `disabled={readOnly}` on every field and the remove button, so no inspector file needed to move. The card's symptom 2 closes through the flag the pillar already documents.
- **The rollback — right; the guard cannot leave a refused status on screen.** On refusal the `setDraft` updater restores only `status` (to `prevDraft.status`, or removes the key when the pre-toggle draft had none, which `flowEnabled` reads as enabled), guarded on `draftFlowRef.current === flowName` and `d.status === nextStatus`. Measured against the triage's bar, "the switch never shows a state the server refused": the two branches that leave the draft untouched are exactly the cases where the refused status is NOT on screen. (a) Another flow is on screen: the load effect on `current` replaced `draft` from the server, and reopening the first flow reloads it from the server too — nothing caches the optimistic draft, so the refused value cannot come back. (b) The on-screen status already differs from the refused value, which is the author's state, not the server-refused one. A second toggle during the in-flight save is impossible (`disabled` on `!!saving`; autosave `blocked` on `!!saving`), so `prevDraft` is always the pre-toggle draft. The one transient I could construct — a refusal landing while a return to the first flow is still loading and the second flow's draft happens to hold the refused status — is overwritten by that load's own `setDraft` when it completes and never reaches a save (the rollback does not set `autoDirty`). The status-only restore is a legitimate refinement of "roll the optimistic draft back": the triage's stated aim is the switch's state, the whole-draft restore would clobber an in-flight inspector edit and rewrite a flow opened during the save, and legs D/E plus the two rollback-shape pins hold both directions. `setSaving(false)` in `finally` re-enables the switch after the rollback; `hasDraft` stays untouched (set only on success) — right.
- **Canvas `onPatch: readOnly ? undefined : onPatch` — right on mechanism; inside the claim's surface, not a breach.** `MetadataPreviewProps` has no `readOnly` prop; its documented read-only lever IS an omitted `onPatch` ("When omitted, the preview surface is read-only"). `FlowPreview` computes `designMode = editing && onSelectionChange` (so selection survives and still opens the inspector, now read-only) and `canEdit = designMode && !!onPatch`; `editable={canEdit}` gates the node palette, the insert-on-edge handle, pointer drag, the Delete key and the append / revise-loop affordances in `FlowCanvas`, and every patch path returns early on `!onPatch`. That is the registry's own contract, and the same "drop the doomed write callbacks on readOnly" shape the Data pillar uses in its `GridFieldAuthoringProvider` value — not a second read-only mechanism. Scope: the card's Expected invokes the pillar's documented `readOnly` contract, "hide/disable flow-authoring affordances"; add / insert / drag / delete on the canvas are flow-authoring affordances of the same pillar, same function, same file. The claim's file surface (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` alone) is unchanged; `FlowPreview.tsx` / `FlowCanvas.tsx` (objectui#10862 slice 4) are untouched; the addition is declared in the PR body, the report and the changeset, with a pin and ablation leg C. Note for the seat: the "four conditions" the dev cites are not rule text I could find in either repo's AGENTS.md or the PM scripts, so this judgment rests on the claim's file surface and the card's Expected — the seat may overrule it from its own rulebook.
- **Pins — right.** The triage's three pins each have a test: read-only switch disabled with the hint and a click saving nothing, plus inspector Label / ID disabled; a refused toggle returning the switch and the canvas status pill to `active` with the refusal shown; the writable control (switch, inspector, canvas all edit; a toggle saves `status: obsolete`). Added: the canvas read-only pin and the two rollback-shape pins. The canvas and the inspector are the real registered `FlowPreview` / `FlowInspector`; the client is a double whose draft save can refuse `403 ITEM_LOCKED` and be held open.
- **Changeset text — right.** Names the three affordances and the rollback exactly as the diff implements them.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/11124-automations-pillar-honours-read-only.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`. The diff publishes no new or changed export, prop, type, accepted value or i18n key — `AutomationsPillar`'s signature is unchanged and the behaviour change is a bug fix on a contract the pillar already documents. Patch is the right level; one changeset for the one released package the diff touches (the test file and the changeset itself publish nothing). Changeset Declaration, Bump Policy, Claim Re-read, Fixed Group Check and Overwrite Report all concluded success on the head.
- `Clause-②: no` — right; it matches the PR body and the claim's own line, and the diff moves no schema, prop, type or accepted set.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation 1 (canvas `onPatch`)** — answered in ①: the preview contract's own read-only lever, the Data pillar's shape, same defect class, same function and file; inside the claim's surface, not a breach.
- **Dev deviation 2 (status-only, same-flow rollback)** — answered in ①: a refinement that meets the triage's bar; the whole-draft restore was the worse reading, and legs D/E pin both directions.
- **Dev deviation 3 (a 4-file unlocked run, later superseded by the full studio-design directory under the lock)** — process only; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts for this record; no bearing on the diff.
- **Dev deviation 4 (a queued lock call moved to the background by the host and waited on in the foreground)** — process only; no watcher left running; no bearing on the diff.
- **Dev deviation 5 (commit trailers follow AGENTS.md's model-free pair rather than the harness reminder)** — verified on the head commit: the `Claude-Session:` line and the `Co-authored-by: Claude` line, no model identifier; that is AGENTS.md's own rule, so right.
- **open_questions** — none declared; none found.
- **Out-of-scope finding (InterfacesPillar)** — real at the head: `Inspector` and `DefaultInspector` are both created with a hardcoded `readOnly={false}` while both of the pillar's autosaves carry `readOnly` in `blocked`, so a surface-inspector edit on a read-only package would take locally and be silently dropped — the same defect class this card closes (a Studio pillar's inspector ignoring the pillar's `readOnly` while its autosave discards the edit). Its `readOnly` doc reads "hide/disable nav-authoring affordances", narrower than the Data / Automations wording, so whether page-inspector edits fall inside that contract is a triage question. Escalated: it needs a carrier — the seat should file a card (source reading only, not yet measured through a public door, so a QA measurement first). It is not this PR's defect and does not bear on this verdict.
- **Check-runs on the head (`filter=latest`)** — 11 were still in progress when this review started (Lint, Spec Main Shape Gate, Test shards 1 to 8, Type Check); waited in the foreground about 8 minutes until every run completed. Final: 43 runs, all completed, 40 success, 3 skipped (the two coverage matrix rows and dependabot, skipped by design), 0 failure, 0 in progress.
